A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FastVID and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–C. Retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark accuracy, inference latency, ablations, and qualitative results, including Qwen2-VL experiments in Appendix B.4.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen2.5-VL experiments, further baseline comparisons, additional analyses, and ANet-QA results.

M1.justification: The DySeg segmentation procedure and STPrune components—density-based merging and attention-based selection—remain intact. Newly documented Qwen frame handling and pseudo-CLS attention do not establish a change to the previously evaluated algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds ANet-QA for the generation evaluation described in Appendix B.4 and Table 12. MVBench, LongVideoBench, MLVU, and VideoMME remain. The additional model configurations and larger frame counts reuse retained benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Table 11 newly evaluates PyramidDrop, SparseVLM, and LLaVA-PruMerge against FastVID on VideoMME; these methods were cited but not evaluated in v2. This substantially broadens the comparator set while retaining the existing comparisons. PyramidDrop also participates in the new ANet-QA evaluation.

E3.justification: v3 adds a Qwen2.5-VL configuration, 128- and 320-frame VideoMME tests with approximately matched input-token budgets, and ANet-QA evaluation using GPT-3.5-Turbo-0125 scoring. It also replaces the unqualified default threshold description with Qwen-specific optimization of tau, without specifying its value or establishing that the unchanged Qwen2-VL results were rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 9–10 add two focused analyses: removing the SigLIP head tests its contribution to ATS, and increasing sampled frames at comparable token budgets tests length extrapolation. Existing component ablations and the hyperparameter analyses in Figures 6–7 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional experiments do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results across new conditions: Qwen2.5-VL scores of 62.8 for FastVID versus 59.3 for PruneVID*; VideoMME scores of 60.4 and 61.4 with 128 and 320 frames; and ANet-QA accuracy/score of 53.1/3.52. It also adds baseline and SigLIP-head results. Matched earlier tables and plots retain their values, apart from equivalent FLOPs rounding; the larger-frame scores are not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the per-segment token allocations from drFN and (1-d)rFN to drPN and (1-d)rPN, making them consistent with the stated rPN total for a P-frame segment. The remaining mathematical development is retained. Changing alpha to beta in Equation 5 only harmonizes notation with the appendix.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain temporal/visual redundancy analysis, the DySeg–STPrune framework, and efficient inference with accuracy preserved under strong compression. The 90.3% pruning, 8.3% FLOPs, 7.1× speedup, and 98.0% accuracy-retention headline is unchanged. Additional model names expand the reported validation of the retained generalization claim.

C2.justification: v3 shifts the explanation of long-video degradation toward query-agnostic retention, interprets existing Figures 8(b) and 9(a) as failure examples, and adds the benefit of KV-cache reuse across dialogue turns. It also discusses SigLIP-head transferability and elaborates why FastVID differs from PruneVID in efficiency and representation preservation.

D1.justification: v3 discloses pseudo-CLS construction for Qwen, the 16384-token cap, and pruning-layer/retention schedules for newly evaluated baselines. It also drops the explicit LLaVA-Video-7B designation. Code access and A100 hardware disclosures remain unchanged, while the newly mentioned optimal Qwen threshold is not numerically specified.

R1.justification: v3 adds eleven references, including Qwen2.5-VL, ActivityNet-QA, LLaVA-MLB, and AdaTP. Appendix C.1 expands the comparison with PruneVID, and Appendix B.3 develops comparisons with previously cited methods. The overall positioning as training-free inference-time spatiotemporal pruning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 streamlines the methodology opening, moves the existing Qwen2-VL discussion into Section 4.2, and adds experiment and discussion subsections. It also standardizes prefill terminology, adds acknowledgments, and edits affiliation information. Most existing prose and the overall section structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds five compact tables, relocates existing displays—including Qwen2-VL from v2 Table 7 to v3 Table 3—and adjusts captions, percentage labels, and boldfacing. Existing figures and plots are retained with minor labeling changes, and the visual presentation is not substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens an already extensively evaluated framework through previously absent baseline comparisons, a direct SigLIP-head control, and additional model, frame-budget, and generation evaluations. The revised failure discussion also clarifies applicability tradeoffs. These are useful incremental gains, although unspecified Qwen settings and limited generation-evaluation details constrain the strength and reproducibility of some additions.
